transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before we get into the Line 4 rinse-recovery discussion, I want to lay out where I stand as Utilities Manager. As we all know, the municipal water-conservation restriction kicks in Monday, which means our current practice of using fresh rinse water on Line 4 each shift is going to be a problem. We've got the closed-loop rinse-recovery skid installed beside Line 4, but it hasn't been placed into production service yet. I'll be making the final utilities authorization and operating-control decision today, but per our standard process, I need to hear from each technical specialist first -- I'll settle the authorization and controls after both technical reviews are formally on the record. So let's get started: what are the findings we need to discuss?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Mara. I've completed commissioning trials on the Line 4 rinse-recovery skid, and I have some important findings to put on the record. My trial data shows that loop conductivity reaches 1,200 microsiemens per centimeter after 40 cycles, which exceeds Line 4's rinse specification of no more than 900. The validated operating plan to stay within spec is to purge exactly 300 liters every 30 cycles. I also confirmed with the skid vendor that pump-seal replacement and recommissioning require exactly 6 hours. However, I need to flag that my trial worksheet is still awaiting engineering signoff. I'll formally disclose each of these findings now so they're on the record for your authorization decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to put my permit review findings on the record. I confirmed with the regulator yesterday that every recovery-loop purge must be neutralized to a pH from exactly 6.5 through 8.5, sampled before discharge, and entered in the wastewater log. I have not yet attached the regulator's note to the utility change record.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Eli's trial worksheet must receive engineering signoff before the system proceeds into production service.

Nadia must attach the regulator's note confirming pH 6.5–8.5 neutralization, pre-discharge sampling, and wastewater log entry requirements to the utility change record before the system proceeds into production service.
